Summary: Jetstream builds an "IDE copilot" platform (VSCode + web IDE) focused on uninterrupted inline completions. Evaluating Redwood for low-latency streaming and token-budget tuning. Priority: user-perceived immediacy for completions inside editor (TTFT is critical).

Recent timeline and touches:
- 2026-01-12: inbound intro, qualified by Morgan. basic requirements doc collected.
- 2026-01-27: demo (Fireflies ff_20260128_jetstream_initial-demo). showed streaming in VSCode prototype; internal feedback: first token appears but follow-on jitter causes caret jumps.
- 2026-02-05: technical deep-dive (Elena + infra). discussed persistent KV cache for file buffers, model pinning, and token budgets for inline vs block completions.
- 2026-02-18: perf triage call (ff_20260218_perf-check). Ran synthetic traces from 50 devs; observed TTFT median ~120ms on Linux staging, tail 95th ~420ms. Mac M1 workstations show higher variance.
- 2026-03-03: security review kickoff. Legal flagged residency and retention; engineering requested KMS + audit log examples.

Technical requirements / buyer-speak (copilot UX):
- TTFT target: <=50ms median for inline single-line completions; <=150ms p95 for multi-line streaming responses.
- Streaming jitter: target <10ms inter-token jitter for smooth animation in the editor (perceptual threshold).
- Token budget: typical inline completion budget 40-80 tokens; multi-line blocks 120-400 tokens. Need per-route token cap and dynamic budget tuning based on latency.
- Backpressure strategy: prefer graceful partial completion (emit prefix) + client-side filler heuristics over dropping; need server acknowledgements for truncation events.
- Model/version pinning: must pin to quantized open models initially; want automated fallback to smaller quantized variant under load while preserving API signature.
- Caching: strong desire for prefix/KV caching keyed by document SHA + workspace context.

POC scope (proposed):
- 2-week Dedicated instance with representative CPU/GPU mix; run synthetic trace of 200 concurrent devs via VSCode extension harness.
- Instrument TTFT, per-token jitter, tail-latency, and token consumption per session.
- Toggle model variants (fp16 -> 4-bit quant) and measure quality delta vs latency.
- Validate SSO/SAML flow and KMS envelope encryption in VPC.
